court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
trial_court: Additional Principal Judge/F.T.C.-II, Mau, in Matrimonial Case No. 665 of 2012
facts_of_case: The parties were married under the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955. The trial court declared their marriage void under Section 12 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955.

legal_principles.principle: When a relationship of marriage is dissolved by decree of court and either no appeal is filed or if filed, is dismissed then either party to the marriage which has been dissolved by the process of law by a decree are free to marry again.
legal_principles.held: The phrase 'either party to the marriage' if is co-related with the first part of the section, marriage which has been dissolved by decree of divorce will indicate that what was provided in this section was that when a relationship of marriage is dissolved by decree of court and either no appeal is filed or if filed, is dismissed then either party to the marriage which has been dissolved by the process of law by a decree are free to marry again.

legal_principles.principle: The legislature so far as decrees under Section 13 are concerned wanted the right of appeal to survive but in decrees under Section 11 or 12 the legislature wanted the right of appeal to be subject to the will of the other party.
legal_principles.held: As it is apparent that if what is contended by the learned counsel for the respondent and held by some of the High Courts is accepted that Section 15 will not apply to cases when a decree is passed under Section 11 or 12 it will mean that as soon as a decree is passed the party aggrieved may appeal but the other party by remarriage would make the appeal infructuous and therefore the right of appeal of one of the parties to the decree under Section 28 will be subject to the act of the other party in cases where decree is passed under Section 11 or 12

outcome.final_order: The appeal was filed within time and the court set aside the order declaring the marriage void.
